repos.title: TaoMate-HD: Progressive-Resolution Autoregressive Audio-Video Generation
repos.paper_summary: TaoMate-HD is an autoregressive model for streaming joint audio-video generation at 768×1376 resolution. Each chunk runs three denoising stages: two on a 480×864 grid and a final one on the 768×1376 grid. Each stage's clean prediction is encoded into a stage-specific key/value history bank for the same stage of the next chunk, so the next chunk can start before the previous one finishes refinement. Continuation training uses overlapping text windows and student-generated rollouts, scored by distribution-matching distillation. The model is a rank-128 LoRA trained on 10,000 distillation pairs over MiniMax-H3. On 100 self-constructed sequences of 1–10 minutes, progressive generation runs 1.60× faster than direct 768p generation (4.68 vs 2.93 FPS, serial). Stage-parallel deployment reaches 8.99 FPS, 1.92× the serial rate. Continuation training lowers character error rate from 30.75% to 19.57%. Limitations: the benchmark uses self-constructed sequences, the parallel configuration has slightly higher CER (21.28%), and serial TaoMate-HD's LipSync (7.061) trails MiniMax-H3 (7.569).

digest_headlines.heading: 1 Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: TaoMate-HD targets high-resolution audiovisual streaming, where dense denoising is costly and text updates can repeat or interrupt speech.

digest_headlines.heading: 2 Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Related work covers few-step distillation, progressive resolution, and stage-parallel inference, which uses history at stage output noise levels.

digest_headlines.heading: 3 Method
digest_headlines.headline: Chunks denoise in two low-resolution steps and one high-resolution step, with each stage's clean prediction reused as history.

digest_headlines.heading: 4 Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Serial TaoMate-HD scores highest on Temporal and AudioAes among streaming generators, reaching 0.913 and 4.407.

digest_headlines.heading: 5 Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The conclusion summarizes gains from progressive denoising and asymmetric distillation, extending to an hour of streaming.

repos.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
repos.paper_summary: The paper presents Megatron-LM, a method for training multi-billion parameter transformer language models using intra-layer model parallelism in PyTorch. The approach partitions the self-attention and MLP blocks across GPUs by splitting weight matrices column-wise for the first linear layer and row-wise for the second, requiring only two all-reduce operations per forward pass. This design avoids custom compilers and is orthogonal to pipeline parallelism. On 512 NVIDIA V100 GPUs, an 8.3 billion parameter GPT-2 model sustains 15.1 PetaFLOPs with 76% scaling efficiency relative to a single-GPU baseline. The same architecture trains a 3.9 billion parameter BERT variant, where rearranging layer normalization before residual connections prevents degradation observed in standard BERT at larger scales. The 8.3B GPT-2 model achieves a WikiText103 perplexity of 10.8 and LAMBADA accuracy of 66.5%, while the 3.9B BERT model reaches 90.9% accuracy on RACE. Limitations include the requirement for high-bandwidth interconnects like NVLink or InfiniBand, and the fact that the BERT results are reported on development sets for most tasks except RACE.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Megatron-LM trains transformers up to 8.3 billion parameters with intra-layer model parallelism, reaching 76% scaling efficiency on 512 GPUs.

digest_headlines.heading: Background and Challenges
digest_headlines.headline: Existing model parallel methods need custom compilers or pipeline changes, so the authors modify only a PyTorch transformer.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Parallel Transformers
digest_headlines.headline: The MLP and attention blocks are split across GPUs so each transformer layer needs only four all-reduce operations.

digest_headlines.heading: Setup
digest_headlines.headline: GPT-2 and BERT models train on an aggregated 174 GB deduplicated corpus with fixed optimizer and learning-rate schedules.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Model parallel scaling reaches 77% of linear scaling at 8.3 billion parameters, and GPT-2 and BERT results set new SOTA marks.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion and Future Work
digest_headlines.headline: The authors conclude that intra-layer parallelism scales to 8.3 billion parameters and suggest hybrid parallelism for larger models.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists BERT finetuning hyperparameters, hybrid parallelism and random number details, text samples, evaluation methodology, and strong scaling results.

repos.title: Kornia: an Open Source Differentiable Computer Vision Library for PyTorch
repos.paper_summary: Kornia is an open-source PyTorch library implementing differentiable computer vision operators for GPU acceleration. The package structures algorithms into modules for color conversion, feature detection, filtering, and geometry, allowing users to embed classical vision tasks directly within neural networks for backpropagation. By using PyTorch's automatic differentiation, the library computes gradients for complex functions like image warping without manual derivative implementation. The authors benchmark Sobel edge detection on 256x256 RGB images using a GTX 1080 Ti, finding that Kornia achieves the best timing performance at large batch sizes on GPU, while CPU performance lags behind optimized libraries like OpenCV. Use cases include image registration via homography optimization and multi-view depth estimation from the SceneNet dataset. Limitations include the assumption of photometric consistency in depth estimation, which restricts accuracy to small view displacements, and the fact that adversarial perturbations demonstrated in feature matching examples are not imperceptible.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Kornia is presented as a PyTorch computer vision library that runs classical image operations on GPUs as differentiable modules.

digest_headlines.heading: Related work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior vision libraries are mostly CPU-based, and deep learning frameworks rely on them for pre- and post-processing.

digest_headlines.heading: Kornia: Computer Vision for PyTorch.
digest_headlines.headline: Kornia is organized into PyTorch-based submodules whose operators are differentiable, batched, device-agnostic and usable across distributed systems.

digest_headlines.heading: Use cases
digest_headlines.headline: Four use cases test the library on Sobel timing, homography registration, depth estimation and adversarial matching.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusions
digest_headlines.headline: Classical vision tasks are reported to solve easily in PyTorch with performance similar to existing libraries.

repos.title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
repos.paper_summary:
Chronos is a pretrained probabilistic time series forecasting framework that adapts standard transformer language models to univariate forecasting. The method converts real-valued time series into discrete tokens by mean-scaling and quantizing values into 4,096 uniform bins. These token sequences are fed into T5 or GPT-2 architectures, which are trained via cross-entropy loss without architectural modifications. The authors pretrain models ranging from 20M to 710M parameters on 28 public datasets augmented with TSMixup convex combinations and KernelSynth Gaussian process synthetic data.

On a benchmark of 42 datasets, Chronos outperforms local statistical models like AutoARIMA and task-specific deep learning baselines such as PatchTST in both in-domain and zero-shot settings. On 27 unseen zero-shot datasets, the 710M parameter model achieves aggregated relative WQL scores comparable to methods specifically trained on those tasks. A limitation is that the fixed vocabulary restricts predictions to the training value range, potentially impairing performance on strongly trending series. Additionally, larger models exhibit slower inference times than lightweight local forecasters.

repos.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
repos.paper_summary: HarnessMM reduces repeated reasoning calls in agent harnesses by storing already-resolved actions as executable decision graphs and replaying them when tool feedback satisfies public guards, with recursive self-improvement refining companion harness configurations. A controller sits at the model–tool boundary and keeps model weights fixed. The method reuses stored actions, with literal arguments, causal dependencies and guards, and calls the original actor again when a new semantic decision, unsupported evidence or abstention occurs. On 98 HumanEval tasks, Codex keeps 90.82% success while Tokens/task (k) fall from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54% saving). DeepSeek Harness rises from 71.43% to 85.71% success while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93% saving). On MBPP, the Qwen-backed DeepSeek Harness rises from 90.27% to 91.83% with Tokens/task (k) falling from 53.98 to 10.61. The paper's stated limitations are that savings depend on provider cache and context accounting, that new semantic decisions still require slow reasoning, and that public-state adapters are task specific. Small development sets leave policy-level quality differences uncertain.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Harnesses re-invoke reasoning after each tool result, even when earlier reasoning already fixed the next action.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior methods reduce, route or reuse calls, while HarnessMM targets whether a future reasoning call must recur.

digest_headlines.heading: Problem Formulation
digest_headlines.headline: Substitution saves cost only when removed reasoning tokens exceed the tokens introduced by authorship, routing and fallback.

digest_headlines.heading: HarnessMM: Reusing Decisions
digest_headlines.headline: Guarded reuse executes stored actions only when public guards hold, and otherwise returns control to the original actor.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: On 98 HumanEval test tasks, HarnessMM keeps Codex success at 90.82% and raises DeepSeek Harness success to 85.71%.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations
digest_headlines.headline: Savings depend on provider accounting and resolved-action availability, and adapters are task specific.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Stored, guard-checked decisions can replace repeated reasoning calls, and companion studies keep their own scope.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix gives per-iteration MiniWoB++ RSI measurements, development protocols, implementation details and paired-effect definitions.

repos.title: ReCache: Learning Budget-Aware Caching Schedules for Diffusion Models via REINFORCE
repos.paper_summary: ReCache learns the step schedule for feature caching in diffusion models, so that the user sets a compute budget k and the policy chooses which k denoising steps get full computation while the rest reuse or forecast cached features. The schedule policy is a budget-conditioned Plackett-Luce distribution over k-subsets, parameterized by an MLP that outputs step-importance logits, and trained with REINFORCE using a leave-one-out baseline and an entropy bonus. The reward combines a distance to full-inference outputs (PLPIPS) and a quality term (HPSv2), so no backpropagation through the diffusion sampler is needed and no labelled data is used. It is combined with TaylorSeer, HiCache, DiCache, and DPCache, and is evaluated on FLUX.1-dev, HunyuanVideo, and Wan2.1. On FLUX.1-dev at 9 steps (5.04× speedup), ReCache with DiCache lowers LPIPS from 0.456 to 0.316 relative to DiCache. On Wan 2.1 at about 2.6× speedup, the paper reports LPIPS falling from 0.480 to 0.169 and VBench rising from 70.4 to 76.0 over uniform HiCache. The paper notes that gains are smallest in low-step regimes (1–4 steps), where caching offers limited benefit.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Hand-crafted caching schedules are replaced by a learned, budget-aware policy trained with reinforcement learning.

digest_headlines.heading: Preliminaries
digest_headlines.headline: Caching splits denoising steps into fully computed steps and reuse steps, with mechanisms that either reuse or forecast features.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: A budget-conditioned policy over step subsets is trained with policy gradients to balance fidelity and reward.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: ReCache outperforms hand-designed schedules on LPIPS and perceptual reward across FLUX.1-dev, HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: ReCache gives limited benefit in one-to-four-step regimes and inherits the safety properties of the underlying model.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers related work, implementation details for baselines and models, extended FLUX results, compute cost, and figures.

repos.title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning
repos.paper_summary: PolicyIK is a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy that learns high-precision inverse kinematics for robot arms through a joint-position interface. The policy accumulates its actions into a joint reference, observes that reference relative to the measured joints, and uses two-scale pose errors with an error-dependent action gain. Its reward combines tracking, a running-best progress term, and a dwell term so the policy both reaches and holds a tolerance of 1 mm and 0.2°. In simulation on a 7-DoF arm, a single attempt by the trained PPO policy keeps mean errors over the final second within tolerance on 93.5% of held-out tasks, rising to 98.9% with a deployment protocol. Ablations show each design choice lowers single-attempt success by 1.8 to 9.2 points when removed. On two physical arms, trained with FlashSAC, PolicyIK reaches and holds more tasks than four classical IK controllers under the same time budgets. In simulated pick-and-place, it executes the end-effector commands of the π0.5 VLA policy with 95.7% success across ten adapted LIBERO-Object tasks. Limitations: the policy's real-arm and pick-and-place results are reported with fewer detailed numbers in the text provided, and inference takes 0.035 ms on CPU against a 33 ms control period.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Policies that output end-effector poses inherit inverse kinematics accuracy, and precise inverse kinematics is hard to build.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior learned reaching controllers reach millimeter to centimeter accuracy, and sub-millimeter results need a classical solver.

digest_headlines.heading: Problem Formulation
digest_headlines.headline: Success is defined as mean errors over the final second within 1 mm and 0.2°, posed as goal-conditioned reinforcement learning.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: The method accumulates actions into a joint reference, scales them by error, and rewards each new best error and every step within tolerance.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: In simulation, one attempt reaches 93.5% strict success, rising to 98.9% with the deployment protocol.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Hardware training with the same terminal-phase design reaches and holds more tasks than all four classical controllers.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists simulation setup, reward and training settings, deployment protocol, baseline tuning, hardware controller settings, and xArm7 results.

repos.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
repos.paper_summary: Sentence-BERT (SBERT) modifies BERT to generate fixed-size sentence embeddings suitable for cosine similarity, reducing the time to find the most similar pair in a collection of 10,000 sentences from approximately 65 hours to about 5 seconds. The method adds a pooling operation to the BERT output and fine-tunes the network using siamese or triplet structures on Natural Language Inference data. On seven Semantic Textual Similarity tasks, SBERT achieves an average Spearman rank correlation of 74.89, outperforming InferSent by 11.7 points and Universal Sentence Encoder by 5.5 points. For supervised STS benchmark evaluation, SBERT reaches 84.67 Spearman correlation, comparable to the BERT cross-encoder baseline of 84.30. On SentEval transfer learning tasks, SBERT improves the average accuracy by 2.1 points over InferSent. A limitation is that SBERT underperforms the BERT cross-encoder on the Argument Facet Similarity dataset in cross-topic settings, where it drops by about 7 points because it cannot directly compare unseen argumentative contexts.

repos.title: ExecuTorch -- A Unified PyTorch Solution to Run AI Models On-Device
repos.paper_summary: ExecuTorch is a PyTorch-native deployment framework that enables local AI model execution on edge devices from microcontrollers to smartphones. It uses `torch.export` to capture models into an Edge Dialect graph with fewer than 300 Core ATen operators, which supports ahead-of-time compilation and backend delegation to specialized hardware like NPUs or GPUs. The system serializes models into `.pte` files for low-overhead runtime execution. On a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra, ExecuTorch achieves up to 1542 tokens/sec prefill throughput on the NPU using Qwen3 0.6B, outperforming llama.cpp (409 tokens/sec) and ONNX Runtime. For vision tasks, it reduces MobileNet V3 inference latency to 0.24 ms on the NPU compared to 8.96 ms in LiteRT. Limitations include difficulty exporting models with data-dependent control flow or dynamic shapes, and AOT compilation requires hardware-specific binaries, increasing deployment complexity across diverse Android devices.

repos.title: Execution-State Capsules: Graph-Bound Execution-State Checkpoint and Restore for Low-Latency, Small-Batch, On-Device Physical-AI Serving
repos.paper_summary: FlashRT is a kernel runtime and execution-state capsule mechanism for low-latency, single-stream on-device inference. It captures the forward pass as a CUDA graph over contiguous static buffers, eliminating block-table indirection. The complete state at any token boundary becomes a fixed set of named device buffers; freezing this set into an "execution-state capsule" enables checkpointing, forking, and rollback via simple buffer copies. On an RTX 5090, FlashRT achieves 2.6–2.8× lower cold time-to-first-token (TTFT) than vLLM on a hybrid linear-attention model. Capsule restore widens TTFT speedup with prefix length, reaching 3.9× at 22k tokens and 27× at 1616k tokens. Correctness is verified as byte-identical stored state and token-identical greedy decode; a KV-only ablation diverges, confirming that recurrent state restoration is required for exact reuse. The system supports LLM agents, robot policy resets, and planner-actor hand-offs under one contract. Limitations include strict binding to specific weights and kernel versions, ill-suitedness for high-concurrency or variable-shape workloads, and lack of distributed cluster support.
